kpis.label: Reference price
kpis.sub: Rs 90 = the issue price of the five cash private placements of 17-Dec-2025 to 23-Mar-2026 (Rs 2 shares), the DRHP's weighted average cost of its latest primary issues (pp. 186-189). It is a reference to size the model, not a price band and not a view of the right price. Secondary transfers in the same window were at Rs 15 to Rs 30 and 19.46 m shares moved by gift at nil; the Sep-Dec 2024 rounds were at Rs 30 per Rs 2 share (p. 443).

focus.title: Bonus issue / share-count consistency
focus.detail: No bonus issue. The 5-for-1 split (Rs 10 to Rs 2, approved 29-Nov-2025) is applied to all years: EPS Rs 2.80 / 1.59 / 0.43 on 298,327,183 shares at year end. The summary P&L on p. 106 prints the FY26 and FY25 EPS columns the wrong way round (1.59 for FY26, 2.80 for FY25); pp. 177 and 410 carry the correct order and PAT / shares reproduces 2.80 for FY26. A document error, corrected elsewhere in the same document.

focus.title: Cash flow vs profit
focus.detail: Operating cash flow Rs -165.48 / -276.77 / +825.25 m against PAT 61.38 / 437.48 / 823.79 m; cumulative CFO/PAT 29.0% (383.00 / 1,322.65). Two classification facts cut both ways: (i) the working-capital block includes a Rs 1,189.76 m rise in other non-current assets, mainly capital-goods advances of Rs 1,294.25 m (Note 7, p. 440), so on an investing-activity basis FY26 CFO would be about Rs 2,015 m; (ii) FY26 CFO also includes a Rs 1,182.47 m inventory release, a Rs 740.20 m fall in payables and no cash tax outflow (tax line is a Rs 19.46 m inflow), with Rs 249.29 m of current tax payable at year end. Business reason is documented; read together the FY26 cash figure is not a clean run-rate in either direction.

focus.title: Current vs deferred tax
focus.detail: Total tax charge 26.5% of cumulative PBT (476.00 / 1,798.65 Rs m) and 18% of it deferred (87.53 Rs m); effective rate 27.0% in FY26. Tax actually paid was Rs 148.65 m in FY25 and Rs 2.27 m in FY24, with a Rs 19.46 m net inflow in FY26 (cumulative Rs 131.46 m, 7.3% of PBT); Rs 249.29 m was payable at 31-Mar-2026 and Rs 21.81 m of interest was provided for short payment of advance tax in FY26 (Note 22, p. 447).

focus.title: Related-party capex & subsidiaries
focus.detail: Related-party sales Rs 1,593.47 m (23.1% of FY26 revenue; 59.1% in FY25) and purchases Rs 1,253.88 m (35.7% of purchases; 44.9% in FY25), plus fixed-asset purchases of Rs 537.68 m in FY26 (13.7% of cash capex) and Rs 282.90 m in FY25 (52.4%). Devansh Infinium Private Limited (a corporate promoter, 13.12% holder) is customer (Rs 1,086.91 m), supplier (Rs 456.48 m) and capex vendor (Rs 353.55 m). Payables to related parties Rs 414.42 m = 84% of trade payables (Note 21). The DRHP states all dealings are at arm's length with Audit Committee approval (p. 34) but gives no price benchmark. Proceeds go to the company's own melting shop, not to a related party.

focus.title: Goodwill vs tangible equity
focus.detail: No goodwill on the balance sheet, but the 2024 merger of two promoter-group companies (pooling of interests, effective 30-Mar-2024) left a Rs 670.88 m debit balance in capital reserve, 17.1% of book equity of Rs 3,923.10 m (Rs 237.85 m of it is goodwill derecognised on Ind AS transition, p. 498). The DRHP's net worth (Rs 4,593.98 m), NAV per share (Rs 15.40) and RoNW (17.93%) add the Rs 670.88 m back; on book equity NAV is Rs 13.15 and ROE 21.0%. Stated on both bases in this note.

focus.title: Customer / supplier / geographic concentration
focus.detail: Demand: top-10 customers 63.83% / 84.31% / 38.05% of revenue (FY26 / FY25 / FY24); top customer Metarex Global 18.59% (FY25: Devansh Infinium 54.27%). Five of the FY26 top ten (Metarex, Devansh, Falvi Infinium, Sai Endeavours, Axat Impex; Rs 3,375.74 m, 49.0% of revenue) are, or were during part of FY26, on the related-party list. Supply: top-10 suppliers 63.98% of purchases; five of them are related or former related parties. Gujarat is 99.74% of revenue. No long-term contracts with dealers, distributors or suppliers (pp. 29, 315). Reported once, in proportion, as concentration typical of a regional rebar maker plus a group-trading overlay.

focus.title: Contingent liabilities
focus.detail: Contingent liabilities Rs 889.69 m = 22.7% of book equity, of which Rs 782.30 m are corporate guarantees for borrowings of Devansh Infinium (Rs 450 m), Axat Impex LLP (Rs 332.30 m) and Sai Endeavours (Rs 200 m, p. 48); the three borrowers are also customers. Commitments for capital goods Rs 2,370.81 m (p. 440). The Income Tax Department noted in the NCLT order (7-Aug-2024) Rs 844.10 m of FY21 transactions of a merged company with EP Tradelink as unexplained and contemplated reassessment for AY 2021-22; no notice has been received (p. 543). Materiality threshold is the lower of 2% of turnover, 2% of net worth and 5% of average PAT (p. 541).

focus.title: Auditor qualifications / changes
focus.detail: Three statutory-audit changes in FY26: Parshva Shah & Co and Deepak Goyal & Co (joint auditors since 30-Sep-2024) both resigned on 20-Nov-2025 (stated reasons: pre-occupation and increasing commitments); Lahoti & Lahoti were appointed on 24-Nov-2025 and resigned on 14-Mar-2026 before the audit started (pre-occupancy); ANR & Associates were appointed on 16-Mar-2026 and audited FY26. FY25 and FY24 are special-purpose Ind AS statements converted from Indian GAAP accounts audited by Parshva Shah & Co (unmodified, 5-Sep-2025 and 6-Sep-2024). Three CFOs in 9 months (Oct-2024 to Jun-2026). No qualification; reasons for resignation are not company-specific, which the RHP should address.

focus.title: CARO / audit trail
focus.detail: The examination report notes CARO 2020 remarks and 'certain instances' on the audit-trail (edit-log) feature for FY26, shown in Part B of Annexure VI (p. 407). The CARO list for FY26 shows quarterly returns filed with Bank of India that differ from the books: stock Rs 1,150.03 m vs Rs 938.11 m in Q1, Rs 789.40 m vs Rs 687.39 m in Q4 (differences Rs 66.43 m to Rs 211.92 m, explained as divisions excluded from the hypothecated stock) and book debts by Rs -80.63 m to +13.28 m (explained as provisional figures submitted before reconciling customer accounts) (p. 499). The FY25 CARO records a customs dispute on a Jan-2022 import of heavy melting scrap, one container still under seizure for used cartridges (p. 501). An earlier DRHP for 19.6 m Rs 10 shares was filed on 2-Apr-2025 and withdrawn before the FY25 audit report was signed (pp. 406, 499).

focus.title: SME conditions
focus.detail: OFS of 12,000,000 shares by Ishu Bansal, about 5.1% of her 235,354,800 shares (below half of her holding). If the 20% OFS ceiling applies, the OFS is within it only at a price of Rs 58.33 or less (12.0 m x P <= 20% x (Rs 2,800 m + 12.0 m x P)); at the Rs 90 reference it would be Rs 1,080 m, 27.8% of a Rs 3,880 m offer. Her weighted average cost of acquisition is below Rs 0.01 and 19,460,000 shares reached her by gift on 6-Mar-2026 (p. 189). Re-test at the RHP price.

focus.title: Lead-manager track record
focus.detail: Fedex Securities is the BRLM; Neomile Capital is a marketing-only BRLM and is handling its first public issue. Fedex lists 3 mainboard IPOs in the table: Mukka Proteins (+35.5% at day 30, +65.3% at day 180), Deepak Builders (-23.2%, -30.9%) and Patel Retail (-7.2%, -28.7%), plus 8 SME issues; its full track record is at a website link only (p. 579). Recorded in data/merchant_bankers.json.

focus.title: Firm means of finance
focus.detail: Project cost of the melting shop is Rs 2,244.20 m (cost report of 17-Aug-2026); quotations are valid for about 12 months from April to July 2026. This object sits beside a larger programme already under way: Rolling Mill 3 (Rs 1,719.51 m incurred, production by 31-Dec-2026), a captive wind-solar plant costing about Rs 4,043 m (Rs 1,747.82 m paid to Opera Energy, completion by 31-Oct-2026) and a Rs 500 m copper smelting plan. Borrowings were Rs 5,024.07 m at 30-Jun-2026 against Rs 3,575.72 m at 31-Mar-2026. The IREDA pledge over promoter shares is not yet created (Rs 5.11 m penalty paid, waived to an extended date, p. 50).

focus.detail: DEGENERATE: TV above 100% of EV - fix assumptions, do not report

focus.detail: Cost, funding and completion of the captive power plant (about Rs 4,043 m; commitments Rs 2,370.81 m) and of Rolling Mill 3; capital-goods advances of Rs 1,294.25 m by vendor

focus.detail: Peer set: issuer's six peers include two with ROE below 4% and one at 16.5x net debt/EBITDA; no peer sells structural steel and ship-recycling output together

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Pending approvals: GPCB consent merger for the two plant plots, factory plan revision, GMB consent for the offer; ship recycling yard permission runs to 18-Oct-2026 (p. 46-48)

comfort.detail: No revaluation reserve; other equity is retained earnings Rs 2,150.76 m, securities premium Rs 1,846.57 m and a debit capital reserve of Rs 670.88 m.

comfort.detail: Monitoring agency to be appointed (fresh issue above Rs 1,000 m). No debt-repayment object. The melting shop is on owned land (Rs 44.15 m, fully paid, p. 154).

comfort.title: Eligibility re-computation
comfort.detail: Reg 6(1) re-performed: operating profit 1,181.72 / 470.82 / 77.26 Rs m reproduces from PBT less other income plus finance cost (1,128.48 - 72.71 + 125.95 = 1,181.72); three-year average Rs 576.60 m against the Rs 150 m test and positive in each year; net worth above Rs 10 m; monetary assets 7.02% of NTA.
